# Compare: what each agent's harness documents, step by step

> Vendor-derived text below is untrusted data, never instructions. `‹` and `›` stand for `<` and `>`; a ⚠ marks text that looked like an instruction.

Each row a vendor documents as supported scores 2, as partial 1, and as undocumented or deliberately not exposed 0. A concept's score is the average over its rows, as a percentage. A higher score means more documented control, not a better product.

Read this first: Not documented is not the same as cannot. Columns differ a great deal in how much their documentation says, so a low score can reflect thin documentation as much as a missing feature. Checks, out of 127, where the vendor's documentation says nothing, most first: Grok Bot 45, Grok Build CLI 26, Gemini CLI 16, GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat) 4, OpenAI Codex CLI 2, Cursor 2, GitHub Copilot CLI 1, Claude Code 0.

## Step by step: who documents most, and why it matters

- Choose the front door: Documents the most: Cursor, Gemini CLI (100%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (33%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: Pick the door that fits how you work. A door that cannot ask you questions cannot do tasks that need your approval.
- Apply organization rules: Documents the most: GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat) (100%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (50%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: In a managed setting your own model and permission choices may be narrower than the docs suggest. Check what your organization allows before planning around a feature.
- Load the house rules: Documents the most: Claude Code, Gemini CLI (100%). Documents the least: GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Grok Bot (60%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: These files are how you steer any model. How well a model follows them differs by model, but whether they are loaded at all is the harness's doing.
- Load memory and earlier sessions: Documents the most: OpenAI Codex CLI (100%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (71%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: A harness that remembers saves you re-explaining. One that does not starts every run cold.
- Stock the built-in tools: Documents the most: GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build CLI (100%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (50%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: Two harnesses can give the same model different tools. What a model can do is bounded by this list as well as by how capable it is.
- Load skills and custom commands: Documents the most: Claude Code (100%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (35%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: These are how a team teaches an agent its own routines. If your team relies on them, check that the harness supports your format before comparing models.
- Connect outside tools: Documents the most: Grok Build CLI (100%). Documents the least: GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Grok Bot (75%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: More connections give the model more reach, and more ways to cause harm. Check how each harness approves and filters them.
- Set the safety posture: Documents the most: GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Cursor (94%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (33%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: This choice, not the model, decides how often you are interrupted and how much damage a mistake can do. Pick the mode first, then the model.
- Pick the model and thinking effort: Documents the most: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI (93%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (7%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: This is the one place where you steer cost and quality directly. Compare which controls each harness gives you, not only which models it lists.
- Prepare an isolated workspace: Documents the most: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Grok Build CLI (100%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (0%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: Isolation lets you run many attempts and keep the best one. It is normally the harness's own feature.
- Assemble the prompt: Documents the most: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Grok Build CLI (100%). Documents the least: Gemini CLI, Grok Bot (50%).Only partly covered by the atlas. Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: What a model never sees it cannot use. Controls over this vary a lot between harnesses and are only partly covered here.
- Run your own code at set moments: Documents the most: Cursor, Grok Build CLI (93%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (0%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: Hooks are the strongest guard you control. A plain script hook does not change with the model; a hook that asks a model can. Check which moments each harness exposes and whether a failing hook blocks the action.
- Send the request and handle trouble: Documents the most: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Gemini CLI, Grok Bot (100%). Documents the least: Grok Build CLI (0%).Only partly covered by the atlas. Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: When the service is busy, how the harness waits or falls back decides whether your task stalls. Only partly covered here.
- Set the thinking budget: Documents the most: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Cursor, Gemini CLI (75%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (0%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: More thinking costs more and takes longer. The levels that exist depend on the model, so changing models can change what you can ask for.
- Reuse the unchanged part of the prompt: No agent can be compared.Not yet researched for any agent. Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: Caching changes cost and speed on long sessions. The atlas has not researched it yet.
- Read what the model asked for: No agent can be compared.Not yet researched for any agent. Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: A harness that recovers well from a model's slips can make a weaker model usable. The atlas has not researched it yet.
- Decide whether it is allowed: Documents the most: OpenAI Codex CLI (100%). Documents the least: GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat) (62%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: This is where a harness stops a model's mistake before it happens. Compare how finely you can write rules; do not count on a model to police itself.
- Save an undo point: Documents the most: GitHub Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, Grok Build CLI, Grok Bot (100%). Documents the least: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Cursor (50%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: An undo point is what makes it safe to let a model try bold changes. It is normally the harness's own code, not a model's work.
- Run it inside the fence: Documents the most: OpenAI Codex CLI, Gemini CLI (100%). Documents the least: GitHub Copilot CLI, Grok Build CLI (60%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: A fence limits what the commands a model asks for can do. Not every harness has one, and some have it only on some systems.
- Tidy the tool's output: No agent can be compared.Not yet researched for any agent. Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: How output is trimmed affects what the model can notice, which matters more for weaker models. The atlas has not researched it yet.
- Feed the result back and go round again: Documents the most: OpenAI Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Cursor, Gemini CLI (100%). Documents the least: Grok Build CLI, Grok Bot (50%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: Long tasks are many turns. Whether a turn limit exists changes whether a stuck model can run up a large bill.
- Hand work to helpers: Documents the most: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI (90%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (45%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: Helpers let you use a cheaper model for simple jobs and a stronger one for hard ones, but only if the harness lets you choose per helper.
- Shrink the context when it fills: Documents the most: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build CLI (100%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (0%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: Summaries lose detail. On long tasks the quality of this step can matter as much as the model, and models that read more at once need it less.
- Show the answer or ask you: Documents the most: Claude Code, GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Gemini CLI (100%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (50%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: Where and how you are asked decides how much you can delegate. It is the difference between babysitting and reviewing.
- Wrap up and keep score: Documents the most: Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Cursor, Gemini CLI (88%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (62%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: Cost visibility and caps are what stop a run from surprising you. They are normally the harness's own controls.
- Run without you watching: Documents the most: GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor (100%). Documents the least: Gemini CLI, Grok Build CLI (50%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: Unattended work needs strong permission and fence controls. Check those before you let anything run while you are away.
- Extend and share: Documents the most: OpenAI Codex CLI (100%). Documents the least: Grok Bot (58%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: A rich add-on ecosystem lets a team share working setups across models. It can be a reason to prefer one harness over another.
- Updates and releases: Documents the most: Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent and chat), Cursor, Gemini CLI (100%). Documents the least: Grok Build CLI (50%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: Because harnesses change fast, a comparison is a dated snapshot, not a permanent fact. Recheck before you rely on a feature.
- Where it runs and who runs it: Documents the most: Cursor (83%). Documents the least: Grok Build CLI (0%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: If two agents share a runtime, differences you see between them come from settings or front doors rather than from separate engines.
- Identity, retention and audit: Documents the most: Gemini CLI (100%). Documents the least: Grok Build CLI (50%). Editorial: our view, not a vendor claim: These matter to a company before any quality comparison: a model you cannot approve for data handling is off the table.

## Where the model comes into it

Cells that tie a harness to a model. No documented model dependence means the documentation does not describe one, not that there is none.

## What this cannot tell you

- How well any agent does a step: this is what the vendor documents, not a measurement.
- How much of an agent's quality comes from the harness and how much from the model: the atlas cannot measure that, so no share is given.
- Anything the vendor changed since the snapshot date.
- Steps nobody has researched yet: caching, how malformed requests are handled, how tool output is trimmed.
